sdk_checked: vLLM main source (git clone --depth 1, commit d187921, 2026-11-08) imported from source in a scratch uv venv (Python 3.12, torch + requirements/common.txt, openai SDK; VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu, no compiled kernels). Every `vllm serve` flag in the post parsed with vllm.entrypoints.common.cli_args.make_arg_parser and the `serve` subcommand parser (config-file precedence checked: positional model beats the YAML `model`); LLM/SamplingParams/LLM.chat/EngineArgs.generation_config, ObservabilityConfig.custom_histogram_buckets validation, KVCacheManager (allocate_slots, get_computed_blocks, free, reset_prefix_cache, take_events), scheduler.py and loggers.py read in source; Prometheus exposition of a Counter named vllm:prefix_cache_hits checked with prometheus_client (exported as vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total). Client blocks and curl commands run against a local fake OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1:18000 (no key) and 127.0.0.1:18001 (keys new-key, old-key); localhost:8000 was taken by an unrelated local process, so base_url was rewritten in scratch copies only. Official docs read from the same commit's docs/ tree (getting_started/quickstart.md, installation/gpu*.md, cpu*.md, deployment, design/metrics.md, usage/metrics.md, serving/parallelism_scaling.md) plus live docs.vllm.ai pages (installation/gpu, stable api kv_cache_manager); arXiv HTML 2309.06180; blog.vllm.ai 2023-06-20. Non-official fetched: robulka.com/vllm, parseable.com vLLM OTel post, discuss.vllm.ai thread 1260 (JSON). Remote image/link URLs checked with curl. All code run with AWS_PROFILE/AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/AWS_SESSION_TOKEN unset and AWS_CONFIG_FILE=AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/dev/null; no weights downloaded, no GPU, no paid model.

score_evidence.A: Problem-first opening without TL;DR; topic headings; internals from L492; ends on alerts (L1286). Valid Markdown and math.
score_evidence.B: Good Korean on re-read; formula boxes and a few padding sentences are the main issues.
score_evidence.C: Two introductions to PagedAttention (L48, L492) and offline/online/backends before mechanisms; transitions within sections are smooth.
score_evidence.D: Excellent toy programs whose traces are correct; padding at L79-81 and L240.
score_evidence.E: Tables, diagram, formulas and code are well placed; backend table weak.
score_evidence.F: Sample hit one wrong number (L640 '약 20%' vs 20-26%); off-sample L123 stale XPU wheel claim and unsourced L1022 attribution.
score_evidence.T1: Re-ran all three toy programs and both clients; all flags parse; only the two unnamed settings keep it short of 9.
score_evidence.T2: Coverage grounded in the sources; installation and build recipes take a disproportionate share.
score_evidence.T3: Deep on mechanisms and observability; missing the 'when to choose / failure modes' synthesis.

writer_assessment_at_end.evidence: The post ends at L1286 with alert-rule advice ('그래도 원인이 보이지 않는 느린 요청은 트레이스로 추적합니다.'); no closing section on when to choose vLLM, its limits or failure modes.

length_fitted.evidence: 1,310 lines. Hard parts get room (block manager, scheduler, histogram interpolation), but installation runs L85-210 with Intel XPU source build, ROCm setup.py, Docker image build from source and QEMU registration (L207-209), and trivial steps get their own block (L79-81 'python3 --version').
